highest_reported.source: Smith and Montemanni, A New Table of Permutation Codes, Table 3 and §4 item 22; current-parameter literature survey checked 2026-11-06.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The published PGL(2,11) group code was independently reconstructed and all 870540 codeword pairs were checked exactly. The surveyed sources did not identify a higher (12,9) code. This is the highest located report, not a claim that all publications have been exhaustively searched.

best_human.source: D. H. Smith and R. Montemanni, A New Table of Permutation Codes, Designs, Codes and Cryptography 63 (2012), Table 3 and §4 item 22; DOI 10.1007/s10623-011-9551-8.
best_human.provenance: Traditional group-theoretic construction using PGL(2,11); the 2011/2012 source predates modern LLM-based generative AI and reports no AI contribution.
best_human.evidence_state: The construction and score are fully reconstructed locally from the projective action on F_11 union {infinity}; exact all-pairs validation confirms 1320 words and minimum distance 10.

best_public.source: Smith and Montemanni, A New Table of Permutation Codes, Table 3 and §4 item 22.
best_public.provenance: Traditional PGL(2,11) construction; no generative AI contribution is reported in this pre-LLM source.
best_public.evidence_state: The paper reports the 1320-element group orbit and internal minimum distance 10. The local witness is an independent reconstruction, not a transcription of the authors' data file.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Replay the saved PGL(2,11) projective actions, then recompute every pairwise Hamming distance with integer comparisons.
best_reproduced.origin_type: independent reconstruction of a published group-theoretic construction

frozen_human_baseline.evidence_state: Same-parameter published human group construction, reconstructed and exactly checked.

optimality_status.status: open; reported bounds 1320 <= M(12,9) <= 11880 in the checked table
optimality_status.evidence: Smith and Montemanni's Table 3 gives lower bound 1320 and upper bound 11880 for (12,9); §4 item 22 supplies a PGL(2,11) code with internal distance 10. Their n=12,d=10 entry is solved at 1320, but that is a separate configuration. Bereg et al. (2025) report new lower bounds for other parameter pairs; their tables do not list (12,9). The current UTD permutation-array index was checked, but its general table endpoint returned HTTP 403; no source checked here reports a proof that M(12,9)=1320.
optimality_status.limitations: The 11880 upper bound is the bound printed in the 2012 table, not certified as the strongest bound available in 2026. The literature survey found no stronger same-parameter lower bound but is not exhaustive.
